Deadly natural disasters of the 20th cen.Messina earthquake: The Sicilian city was almost completely destroyed by an earthquake and tsunami that killed tens of thousands of people.
Deadly natural disasters of the 20th cen.Haiyuan earthquake: One of the deadliest earthquakes in history struck China's Ningxia region, killing an estimated 200,000 people in landslides.
Deadly natural disasters of the 20th cen.Great Kantō earthquake: The quake destroyed much of Tokyo and Yokohama, and the fires that followed caused most of the roughly 100,000 deaths.
Deadly natural disasters of the 20th cen.China floods: The Yangtze and Yellow River floods are among the deadliest natural disasters ever recorded, killing millions.
Deadly natural disasters of the 20th cen.Bhola cyclone: One of the deadliest tropical cyclones ever, it struck the Ganges delta in then East Pakistan and helped trigger the independence of Bangladesh.
Deadly natural disasters of the 20th cen.Tangshan earthquake: This quake in northern China killed hundreds of thousands, one of the deadliest earthquakes of the century.
Deadly natural disasters of the 20th cen.Armero mudflow: The eruption of Nevado del Ruiz melted glaciers and sent a huge mudflow that buried the Colombian town of Armero.
Deadly natural disasters of the 20th cen.Bangladesh cyclone: A powerful cyclone struck the Chittagong coast, killing well over 100,000 people in Bangladesh.
Deadly natural disasters of the 20th cen.Hurricane Mitch: This storm brought catastrophic flooding and mudslides to Honduras and Nicaragua, killing thousands.
Deadly natural disasters of the 20th cen.Vargas mudslides, Venezuela: Heavy rains on the coast of Venezuela triggered landslides that killed tens of thousands and wiped out entire towns.

When these places switched or reformed t.Serbia (Vuk's Cyrillic): Vuk Karadžić reformed Cyrillic with the rule write as you speak and read as it is written, making Serbian highly phonetic.
When these places switched or reformed t.Romania (to Latin): The Romanian language dropped Cyrillic for a Latin script, highlighting its Romance roots.
When these places switched or reformed t.Albania (Latin alphabet): The Congress of Manastir standardized one alphabet for a language that had been written in Arabic, Greek and Latin scripts.
When these places switched or reformed t.Turkey (to Latin): Atatürk personally taught the new alphabet in public squares, and literacy rose dramatically.
When these places switched or reformed t.Mongolia (to Cyrillic): Under Soviet influence, Cyrillic replaced the traditional vertical script, which Mongolia is now reviving.
When these places switched or reformed t.Somalia (Latin script): After years with no official script, the government chose Latin letters and launched a major literacy campaign.
When these places switched or reformed t.Moldova (back to Latin): A law switched Romanian-language Moldova back to Latin, while the breakaway Transnistria still uses Cyrillic.
When these places switched or reformed t.Azerbaijan (back to Latin): This country went from Latin to Cyrillic in 1939 and back to Latin after the Soviet breakup.
When these places switched or reformed t.Uzbekistan (to Latin): It planned a Latin shift for years, and the deadline has been repeatedly delayed.
When these places switched or reformed t.Kazakhstan (to Latin): The president's plan for a Latin alphabet was revised after criticism of its use of apostrophes.

Snooker world champions, by first title.Joe Davis: He won the first world championship in 1927 and retired unbeaten in 1946, having claimed 15 titles.
Snooker world champions, by first title.Fred Davis: Joe's younger brother, he won the snooker title in 1948 and later became a world billiards champion too.
Snooker world champions, by first title.Ray Reardon: A former Welsh miner and policeman nicknamed Dracula for his widow's peak, he won six titles in the 1970s.
Snooker world champions, by first title.Alex Higgins: The Hurricane won as a 23-year-old in 1972, then again in 1982; his fast, reckless style drew huge TV audiences.
Snooker world champions, by first title.Steve Davis: He dominated the 1980s with six titles; his 1985 final, lost on the last black, drew roughly 18 million UK viewers.
Snooker world champions, by first title.Stephen Hendry: He became the youngest world champion ever, at 21, in 1990.
Snooker world champions, by first title.John Higgins: A Scot and a four-time champion, he first won the title in 1998 and has been a fixture at the top for decades.
Snooker world champions, by first title.Ronnie O'Sullivan: The Rocket holds the fastest maximum break, 147 in 5 minutes 8 seconds, made in 1997.
Snooker world champions, by first title.Mark Selby: Nicknamed the Jester from Leicester, he is known for relentless safety play and gritty comebacks.
Snooker world champions, by first title.Judd Trump: Nicknamed the Ace in the Pack for daring potting, he beat John Higgins 18-9 in the 2019 final.

How long these take to grow before harve.Bean sprouts: They can be grown in a jar without soil, and they are usually mung beans.
How long these take to grow before harve.Microgreens: Chefs harvest tiny seedlings just after the first true leaves appear, and the habit spread through restaurants in the 1980s.
How long these take to grow before harve.Radishes: One of the fastest garden vegetables; its sharp heat comes from the same compounds as mustard and wasabi.
How long these take to grow before harve.Lettuce: Its name derives from the Latin lac for milk, after the sap, and ancient Egyptians already grew it.
How long these take to grow before harve.Carrots: Early carrots were purple or yellow; orange varieties took off in the Netherlands.
How long these take to grow before harve.Potatoes: Domesticated in the Andes thousands of years ago, it reached Europe in the 1500s, and many people distrusted it at first.
How long these take to grow before harve.Pumpkins: Botanically a fruit, it is a kind of squash, and giant ones can weigh over a tonne.
How long these take to grow before harve.Garlic: Planted in autumn as a clove and harvested in summer, garlic was found in Tutankhamun's tomb.
How long these take to grow before harve.Asparagus (first harvest): A bed needs a couple of years of patience before the first harvest, then produces for 15 to 20 years.
How long these take to grow before harve.Apple tree (first fruit): Grown from seed it would be unpredictable, which is why growers graft; the first apples take years.

The Ottoman Empire, rise to fall.Suleiman becomes sultan: Suleiman the Magnificent expanded the empire and was known as the Lawgiver to his own people, and his reign is seen as a golden age.
The Ottoman Empire, rise to fall.First Siege of Vienna: The first Siege of Vienna was a failure, and it marked the farthest reach of Ottoman advance into Central Europe at the time.
The Ottoman Empire, rise to fall.Battle of Lepanto: The Battle of Lepanto was one of the largest naval battles of the era, and it involved fleets of galleys, and the writer Cervantes was wounded there.
The Ottoman Empire, rise to fall.Battle of Vienna: The Battle of Vienna ended in a defeat for the Ottomans, and legend says the croissant was invented to celebrate.
The Ottoman Empire, rise to fall.Treaty of Karlowitz: The Treaty of Karlowitz was the first time the Ottomans ceded major territory, and it marked the start of their decline.
The Ottoman Empire, rise to fall.Tanzimat reforms begin: The Tanzimat reforms attempted to modernize the empire, and they introduced new laws and equal rights for subjects.
The Ottoman Empire, rise to fall.Young Turk Revolution: The Young Turk Revolution restored the constitution and forced the sultan to share power, and it led to a new era.
The Ottoman Empire, rise to fall.Gallipoli campaign: Gallipoli saw the Ottomans repel a large Allied landing, and it is a defining national moment for Turkey, Australia and New Zealand.
The Ottoman Empire, rise to fall.Sultanate abolished: The Sultanate's abolition ended six centuries of Ottoman rule, and the last sultan left the country on a British warship.
The Ottoman Empire, rise to fall.Caliphate abolished: The abolition of the Caliphate ended a religious institution that had existed for centuries, and Ataturk's reforms continued.

Book publishers, by founding year.Longman: Longman is one of the oldest publishing houses in the English language, and it later became known for dictionaries.
Book publishers, by founding year.John Murray: John Murray published Byron and Jane Austen, and it was based on Albemarle Street in London.
Book publishers, by founding year.Harper (Harper & Row): Harper & Brothers began in New York, and its magazine Harper's is America's oldest continuously published monthly.
Book publishers, by founding year.Macmillan: Macmillan was founded in Scotland by two brothers, and it published Lewis Carroll's Alice in Wonderland.
Book publishers, by founding year.Mills & Boon: Mills & Boon built a name for romance novels, and its books are known for happy endings.
Book publishers, by founding year.Scholastic: Scholastic sells books to schools, and it publishes the Harry Potter series in the United States.
Book publishers, by founding year.Simon & Schuster: Simon & Schuster's first publication was a crossword puzzle book, and it started a craze for crosswords.
Book publishers, by founding year.Random House: Random House got its name because its founders said they would publish a random lot of books.
Book publishers, by founding year.Penguin Books: Penguin Books revolutionized publishing by making quality paperbacks cheap, and Allen Lane launched it after a train journey.
Book publishers, by founding year.Bloomsbury: Bloomsbury published Harry Potter in the UK, and it was named after the London district associated with writers.

How many does each have?.Keys on a phone keypad: Bell Labs tested layouts and settled on this grid, which puts 1-2-3 on top, unlike calculators with 7-8-9 on top.
How many does each have?.Holes on a golf course: The standard 18 holes come from St Andrews in Scotland, which settled on 18 after merging shorter holes around 1764.
How many does each have?.Pips on a die: Opposite faces of a standard die always sum to seven, so the pips pair up as 1-6, 2-5 and 3-4.
How many does each have?.Monopoly title deeds: Twenty-two streets, four railroads and two utilities make up the properties players can buy.
How many does each have?.Black keys on a piano: Black keys come in groups of two and three, which helps pianists orient themselves across the keyboard.
How many does each have?.Spaces on a Monopoly board: The board's four corners are Go, Jail, Free Parking and Go to Jail, and the game grew from Lizzie Magie's Landlord's Game.
How many does each have?.Weeks in a year: A year is 52 weeks plus a day, or two in a leap year, which is why a date's weekday shifts each year.
How many does each have?.Stickers on a Rubik's Cube: Six faces with nine stickers each, yet the cube has over 43 quintillion possible arrangements.
How many does each have?.Keys on a piano: They span a little over seven octaves, whereas early pianos had far fewer keys, often around 60.
How many does each have?.Keys on a full-size keyboard: The 104-key layout is standard for full-size Windows keyboards, extending the older 101-key design of 1986.

First sightings of cryptids and creeps.Loch Ness Monster (St Columba): A medieval biography of St Columba says he faced a beast in the River Ness, centuries before the monster craze.
First sightings of cryptids and creeps.Jersey Devil: Legend says it was a Pine Barrens woman's thirteenth child, and the NHL's New Jersey Devils are named for it.
First sightings of cryptids and creeps.Abominable Snowman (name): The name came from journalist Henry Newman, who rendered a Tibetan term for a wild man of the snows.
First sightings of cryptids and creeps.Flying saucers (Arnold): Pilot Kenneth Arnold reported nine shining objects near Mount Rainier, and a reporter's phrase flying saucer stuck.
First sightings of cryptids and creeps.Flatwoods Monster: Residents of Flatwoods, West Virginia, reported a tall hooded creature after a meteor passed in September.
First sightings of cryptids and creeps.Bigfoot (name): The name emerged after huge footprints appeared at a California logging site, and the family of a prankster later admitted faking them.
First sightings of cryptids and creeps.Mothman: Reports of a red-eyed winged creature in Point Pleasant, West Virginia, preceded the Silver Bridge collapse in December 1967.
First sightings of cryptids and creeps.Dover Demon: Teenagers in Dover, Massachusetts, reported a big-headed creature over just a couple of nights in April.
First sightings of cryptids and creeps.Chupacabra: First reported in Puerto Rico, the goat-sucker was blamed for livestock deaths, and many described carcasses were mangy coyotes.
First sightings of cryptids and creeps.Slender Man: Created in a 2009 online forum contest by Eric Knudsen, it grew into a famous internet horror legend.

Geological periods: when did each one be.Cambrian: The oldest period of the Phanerozoic saw an explosion of animal life, and in it most major animal groups first appear in the fossil record.
Geological periods: when did each one be.Ordovician: Life stayed in the seas, and the first jawless fish and early corals spread; it ended with one of the big five mass extinctions.
Geological periods: when did each one be.Silurian: It saw the first vascular land plants, and its name comes from the Silures, a Welsh tribe, reflecting the rocks first studied in Wales.
Geological periods: when did each one be.Devonian: The 'Age of Fishes' saw armored giants like Dunkleosteus, and the first four-legged animals, tetrapods, crawled onto land.
Geological periods: when did each one be.Carboniferous: Its name means 'coal-bearing', since vast swampy forests of this time later turned into much of the world's coal.
Geological periods: when did each one be.Permian: Ended with the worst mass extinction in Earth's history, wiping out about 90 percent of marine species, in the event called 'the Great Dying'.
Geological periods: when did each one be.Triassic: It was the dawn of dinosaurs and early mammals, and the supercontinent Pangaea began to break apart.
Geological periods: when did each one be.Jurassic: Named for the Jura Mountains on the French-Swiss border, it's the age of Stegosaurus and Brachiosaurus, and early birds like Archaeopteryx appear.
Geological periods: when did each one be.Cretaceous: Its name comes from the Latin for chalk, 'creta', since white cliffs, like Dover's, formed from the shells of tiny plankton.
Geological periods: when did each one be.Paleogene: It began after the asteroid impact killed off non-avian dinosaurs, and the time of mammals started, though its name means 'ancient-born'.

The Minor Prophets, in Bible order.Hosea: Hosea was told to marry an unfaithful wife as a living picture of Israel's faithlessness, and he is the only northern-kingdom prophet with a book.
The Minor Prophets, in Bible order.Joel: Joel describes a devastating locust plague; Peter quoted his promise that God's spirit would be poured out on all people in his Pentecost sermon.
The Minor Prophets, in Bible order.Amos: Amos was a shepherd and fig farmer from Judah who traveled north to denounce injustice, making him one of the earliest prophets whose words were written down.
The Minor Prophets, in Bible order.Obadiah: At just one chapter, Obadiah is the shortest book in the Hebrew Bible, a fierce oracle against the neighboring nation of Edom.
The Minor Prophets, in Bible order.Jonah: Jonah is the only prophet in this group famous for a story rather than sermons: he fled by sea, was swallowed by a great fish, and sulked when Nineveh repented.
The Minor Prophets, in Bible order.Micah: Micah foretold that a ruler would come out of little Bethlehem, a line later read at Christmas, and summed up faith as doing justice and walking humbly.
The Minor Prophets, in Bible order.Nahum: Nahum celebrates the fall of Nineveh, the very city Jonah had once been sent to warn; it fell to Babylonians and Medes in 612 BC.
The Minor Prophets, in Bible order.Habakkuk: Habakkuk is unusual for arguing with God, asking why evil goes unpunished, and the book ends with a hymn of trust even if the fields fail.
The Minor Prophets, in Bible order.Haggai: Haggai's few short messages, dated to the month and day, urged returned exiles to rebuild the Jerusalem Temple around 520 BC.
The Minor Prophets, in Bible order.Malachi: Malachi means 'my messenger'; his book closes the Protestant Old Testament with a promise that Elijah will return before the great day of the Lord.

Milestones in the history of tea.Shennong finds tea (legend): Legend says leaves from a wild tree fell into the pot of boiling water of the divine farmer.
Milestones in the history of tea.Lu Yu's The Classic of Tea: Called the Sage of Tea, his book is the first monograph on tea.
Milestones in the history of tea.Eisai brings tea to Japan: The Zen monk is also credited with bringing the powdered tea tradition that led to matcha.
Milestones in the history of tea.Dutch bring tea to Europe: The Dutch East India Company brought the first tea cargoes to Europe.
Milestones in the history of tea.Boston Tea Party: Colonists dumped 342 chests of tea into Boston Harbor in protest.
Milestones in the history of tea.Assam tea plant identified: Robert Bruce found the native tea plant in Assam, a different variety from the Chinese one.
Milestones in the history of tea.Afternoon tea becomes a thing: Anna, Duchess of Bedford, is credited for it, as she craved a snack in the long gap before late dinner.
Milestones in the history of tea.Lipton tea brand: Thomas Lipton, a Glasgow grocer, sold tea straight from plantation to cup.
Milestones in the history of tea.Iced tea at St. Louis fair: The St. Louis World's Fair popularized iced tea, supposedly in a heat wave.
Milestones in the history of tea.Bubble tea in Taiwan: Tapioca pearls were added to tea there, though which city invented it is disputed.

When these sports were born.Rugby (Webb Ellis legend): Legend says schoolboy William Webb Ellis picked up the ball at Rugby School, but historians doubt that it happened.
When these sports were born.Baseball's first recorded game: The Knickerbockers played this game in Hoboken, New Jersey, and lost 23 to 1.
When these sports were born.First indoor ice hockey game: Played at Montreal's Victoria Skating Rink, it used a flat wooden block rather than a rubber puck.
When these sports were born.Basketball: James Naismith nailed up peach baskets in Springfield, Massachusetts, and wrote 13 rules for the game.
When these sports were born.Volleyball: William Morgan invented it as 'Mintonette', a gentler alternative to basketball, in Holyoke, Massachusetts.
When these sports were born.Futsal: Created in Montevideo by Juan Carlos Ceriani, its name blends Spanish and Portuguese words for indoor football.
When these sports were born.Pickleball: Legend credits either a boat or a dog named Pickles for the name; it was invented in Washington State.
When these sports were born.Ultimate Frisbee: It began among students in New Jersey and runs on 'Spirit of the Game', with players refereeing themselves.
When these sports were born.Triathlon: Early races in San Diego's Mission Bay inspired it, followed by the Hawaii Ironman in 1978.
When these sports were born.Paintball: The first game was played in the woods of New Hampshire with 12 players and markers made to label trees.

How heavy is the egg?.Ruby-throated hummingbird: The egg is about the size of a pea, though the bee hummingbird's is even smaller.
How heavy is the egg?.American robin: The blue of the robin's egg comes from the pigment biliverdin, which also tints a bruise as it heals.
How heavy is the egg?.Japanese quail: Each quail hen lays eggs with her own unique speckle pattern, so a farmer could tell which hen laid which egg.
How heavy is the egg?.Rock pigeon: Both pigeon parents feed their chicks 'crop milk', a cheesy secretion rich in protein and fat made in the throat.
How heavy is the egg?.Chicken: A hen lays about one egg every 25 hours, and the shell colour is linked to breed.
How heavy is the egg?.Domestic goose: A goose egg is nearly three times a chicken's, and its shell is thick and hard enough to need a solid knock.
How heavy is the egg?.King penguin: A parent balances a single egg on its feet, under a fold of belly skin, with no nest at all.
How heavy is the egg?.Emu: The dark green eggs are incubated by the male for about eight weeks, with almost no food.
How heavy is the egg?.Ostrich: The largest egg of any living bird is equal to about two dozen chicken eggs.
How heavy is the egg?.Elephant bird (extinct): The eggs of Madagascar's giant bird, extinct for about a thousand years, held over 100 chicken eggs' worth.

Graphics cards by release.3dfx Voodoo: It needed a pass-through cable from a separate 2D card, and it dominated early 3D gaming.
Graphics cards by release.Nvidia Riva TNT: TNT stands for TwiNTexel, a feature that processed two textures at once, and the chip combined 2D and 3D in one.
Graphics cards by release.GeForce 256: Nvidia marketed it as the world's first GPU, and the term has stuck ever since.
Graphics cards by release.ATI Radeon (first): ATI created the Radeon brand, and AMD bought the company in 2006.
Graphics cards by release.GeForce 8800 GTX: It was the first DirectX 10 card, with unified shaders, and it helped open up general-purpose computing with CUDA.
Graphics cards by release.GeForce GTX 1080: Built on the Pascal architecture, it was strong enough that many owners kept it for five years or more.
Graphics cards by release.GeForce RTX 2080: These were the first consumer cards with dedicated ray-tracing cores and AI tensor cores.
Graphics cards by release.GeForce RTX 3090: With 24 GB of memory it was marketed as a BFGPU, a big ferocious GPU, by Nvidia's CEO.
Graphics cards by release.GeForce RTX 4090: It can draw up to 450 watts, and some owners suffered melted power connectors.
Graphics cards by release.GeForce RTX 5090: Built on Nvidia's Blackwell architecture, it has 32 GB of GDDR7 memory and arrived in January 2025.

Electromagnetic waves by wavelength.Gamma ray: Emitted by radioactive decay and cosmic explosions, gamma-ray bursts are among the most energetic events known.
Electromagnetic waves by wavelength.X-ray: Wilhelm Rontgen discovered them in 1895, and his first X-ray image was of his wife's hand.
Electromagnetic waves by wavelength.Visible light: Our eyes see only a tiny sliver of the spectrum, about 400 to 700 nanometers.
Electromagnetic waves by wavelength.Body-heat infrared: Thermal cameras and pit vipers detect it.
Electromagnetic waves by wavelength.Big Bang afterglow (CMB): The wavelength of the microwave background, remnant of the early universe.
Electromagnetic waves by wavelength.Microwave oven: Percy Spencer noticed in the 1940s that a chocolate bar had melted in his pocket near radar equipment.
Electromagnetic waves by wavelength.FM radio: FM carries stereo and is less prone to static than AM, but its signal travels mostly in line of sight.
Electromagnetic waves by wavelength.AM radio: At night, AM waves reflect off the ionosphere and can travel hundreds of kilometers.
Electromagnetic waves by wavelength.Submarine VLF radio: It penetrates seawater, and navies use it to send messages to submarines.
Electromagnetic waves by wavelength.50 Hz power-line hum: Europe's mains electricity alternates at 50 Hz, so one full wave would stretch about 6,000 kilometers, roughly the width of the Atlantic.

Fill in the missing number in the title.The ___ Musketeers: The novel is actually about four: d'Artagnan joins the three Musketeers.
Fill in the missing number in the title.Slaughterhouse-___: Vonnegut based it on surviving the Dresden firebombing as a prisoner of war sheltering in a slaughterhouse.
Fill in the missing number in the title.Ocean's ___: The 1960 Rat Pack original was remade in 2001 with George Clooney.
Fill in the missing number in the title.Catch-___: Joseph Heller's no-win paradox gave the language a new phrase.
Fill in the missing number in the title.The ___ Steps: John Buchan's novel was turned into a Hitchcock thriller in 1935.
Fill in the missing number in the title.Around the World in ___ Days: Jules Verne's Phileas Fogg bets £20,000 that he can go around the world in this time.
Fill in the missing number in the title.___ Dalmatians: Dodie Smith wrote the 1956 novel, and Disney's 1961 animation made it famous.
Fill in the missing number in the title.Fahrenheit ___: Ray Bradbury titled it for the temperature at which book paper supposedly catches fire.
Fill in the missing number in the title.(___) Days of Summer: Told out of order, this romantic comedy has a bittersweet ending.
Fill in the missing number in the title.___ Leagues Under the Sea: A league is about four kilometers; the number refers to distance traveled, not depth.

Tall, taller, tallest mountains (anywher.Ben Nevis: The UK's highest peak is cloud-covered most days; a weather observatory ran on its summit until 1904.
Tall, taller, tallest mountains (anywher.Mount Kosciuszko: Polish explorer Strzelecki named it in 1840 for Tadeusz Kościuszko, because the shape reminded him of a mound in Kraków.
Tall, taller, tallest mountains (anywher.Mount Fuji: This sacred volcano last erupted in 1707, and climbers traditionally ascend overnight to watch the sunrise from the summit.
Tall, taller, tallest mountains (anywher.Mont Blanc: The highest Alp changes height with the snow cap, so its figure is approximate; it was first climbed in 1786.
Tall, taller, tallest mountains (anywher.Kilimanjaro: Africa's highest peak is a freestanding volcano rather than part of a range, and its glaciers have shrunk dramatically in a century.
Tall, taller, tallest mountains (anywher.Aconcagua: The tallest mountain outside Asia, in Argentina's Andes, it requires no technical climbing but punishes with altitude and wind.
Tall, taller, tallest mountains (anywher.Everest: Named after surveyor Sir George Everest, it is Chomolungma in Tibetan and Sagarmatha in Nepali, and it rises a few millimeters each year.
Tall, taller, tallest mountains (anywher.Mauna Kea (base to peak): Measured from its base on the sea floor, it is taller than Everest, though only about 4,200 meters show above water; its summit hosts observatories.
Tall, taller, tallest mountains (anywher.Boösaule Montes (Io): Io is the most volcanically active body in the solar system, and its mountains are crustal blocks thrust upward rather than volcanoes.
Tall, taller, tallest mountains (anywher.Olympus Mons (Mars): The solar system's tallest known volcano is about 600 km wide, roughly the size of Arizona, and its slope is so gentle you couldn't see its edge from the summit.

Poems and poetic forms, by number of lin.Haiku: Bashō's frog leaping into an old pond is the most famous example of this Japanese form, which traditionally includes a seasonal word.
Poems and poetic forms, by number of lin.Limerick: Edward Lear popularized this bouncy AABBA form in the 1800s, and it has been the default shape for silly verse ever since.
Poems and poetic forms, by number of lin.Triolet: This French form repeats its first line as the fourth and seventh, and its second line as the eighth, so little new text is needed.
Poems and poetic forms, by number of lin.Shakespearean sonnet: Shakespeare wrote 154 of these, and most end with a rhyming couplet that delivers a twist or sums up the argument.
Poems and poetic forms, by number of lin.Villanelle: Dylan Thomas's "Do not go gentle into that good night" is the best-known one, with two refrains woven through its 19 lines.
Poems and poetic forms, by number of lin.Sestina: Troubadours invented it: six end-words recur in a shifting order across six stanzas, then a short closing envoi uses all of them.
Poems and poetic forms, by number of lin.Ode on a Grecian Urn: Keats wrote this in 1819, and it ends with the famous claim that "Beauty is truth, truth beauty."
Poems and poetic forms, by number of lin.The Raven: Poe's 1845 poem about a croaking bird made him famous, though he reportedly earned only a few dollars from it.
Poems and poetic forms, by number of lin.The Waste Land: T. S. Eliot's 1922 landmark was heavily edited by Ezra Pound, and it quotes lines in several languages without translation.
Poems and poetic forms, by number of lin.Beowulf: This Old English epic about the monster Grendel survives in a single manuscript that was damaged in a 1731 library fire.

The Space Shuttle era.Enterprise glide tests: This test shuttle never reached space. Star Trek fans' letters persuaded NASA to name it Enterprise.
The Space Shuttle era.Columbia's first flight: STS-1 launched on April 12, 1981, exactly 20 years after Yuri Gagarin's flight, with just two astronauts aboard.
The Space Shuttle era.Discovery's first flight: Discovery flew 39 missions, more than any other orbiter, and is now on display near Washington, D.C.
The Space Shuttle era.Atlantis's first flight: This orbiter flew the final Shuttle mission in 2011, and is displayed at Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
The Space Shuttle era.Challenger disaster: It broke apart 73 seconds after launch, because cold weather caused a failed rocket seal. Teacher Christa McAuliffe was among the seven crew lost.
The Space Shuttle era.Hubble deployed: Discovery released the telescope, whose mirror was flawed. A 1993 Shuttle repair mission fitted corrective optics.
The Space Shuttle era.Endeavour's first flight: Built to replace Challenger, it was named after Captain Cook's ship, in a contest among schoolchildren.
The Space Shuttle era.First docking with Mir: Atlantis docked with the Russian space station, which was a landmark of cooperation between former Cold War rivals.
The Space Shuttle era.Columbia disaster: A piece of foam insulation damaged the wing at launch, and the shuttle broke up on re-entry, killing all seven crew.
The Space Shuttle era.Final Shuttle landing: Atlantis closed the 30-year programme, which had flown 135 missions in total.

3D shapes by number of edges.Tetrahedron: The simplest of the Platonic solids has four faces, and it is the only one of the five with no parallel faces.
3D shapes by number of edges.Square pyramid: The pyramids of Egypt have this shape, and each real pyramid has a square base with four sloping triangles.
3D shapes by number of edges.Triangular prism: Newton used a glass one of these to split white sunlight into a rainbow, then used a second prism to recombine it.
3D shapes by number of edges.Pentagonal pyramid: It is the cap you could slice off an icosahedron, and when its faces are regular it counts as a Johnson solid.
3D shapes by number of edges.Cube: Dice are this shape, and on a standard one the opposite faces always sum to seven, so one sits across from six.
3D shapes by number of edges.Pentagonal prism: Its five-sided cross-section is used in the pentaprism of SLR cameras, which flips the image for the viewfinder.
3D shapes by number of edges.Hexagonal prism: The basalt columns of Ireland's Giant's Causeway are mostly this shape, formed as lava cooled and cracked evenly.
3D shapes by number of edges.Octagonal prism: Many church towers, baptismal fonts and pagodas have this form, which suits eight-sided symmetry.
3D shapes by number of edges.Icosahedron: Its 20 faces make the D20 die of tabletop games, and many viruses build their shells in this shape.
3D shapes by number of edges.Truncated icosahedron: This is the shape of a classic soccer ball, with 12 pentagons and 20 hexagons, and also of the carbon molecule buckyball.

Big moments in animal history.Cambrian explosion: Animals suddenly diversified into most of the major body plans we know today, preserved in fossil beds like the Burgess Shale.
Big moments in animal history.End-Ordovician extinction: Glaciation and falling sea levels wiped out about 85 percent of species, making it one of the five great mass extinctions.
Big moments in animal history.First land animals: A tiny millipede called Pneumodesmus, found in Scotland, is the oldest known animal to breathe air on land.
Big moments in animal history.Late Devonian extinction: This wave of extinctions hit reef builders and armoured fish hard, around the time four-legged animals were first leaving the water.
Big moments in animal history.The Great Dying: The Permian-Triassic extinction killed roughly 90 percent of marine species, probably set off by huge volcanic eruptions in Siberia.
Big moments in animal history.First dinosaurs: Early dinosaurs like Eoraptor and Herrerasaurus were small, fast bipeds living in what is now Argentina.
Big moments in animal history.End-Triassic extinction: This extinction cleared out many rival reptile groups, opening the way for dinosaurs to dominate the next 135 million years.
Big moments in animal history.Dinosaur-killing asteroid: The impact formed the Chicxulub crater in Mexico, about 180 km wide, and birds are the dinosaurs that survived.
Big moments in animal history.Eohippus, the dawn horse: This fox-sized, four-toed forest animal, now called Hyracotherium, is the ancestor of horses.
Big moments in animal history.Mainland mammoths vanish: A dwarf population lived on Wrangel Island until about 4,000 years ago, when Egypt's pyramids were already old.

Hot and cold spots of planet Earth.Vostok Station record low: Recorded in July 1983 at a Russian base in Antarctica, it is the lowest air temperature ever reliably measured on Earth.
Hot and cold spots of planet Earth.Oymyakon record low: This Siberian village is the coldest permanently inhabited place; locals leave car engines running so they don't freeze solid.
Hot and cold spots of planet Earth.Average ocean surface: The ocean covers about 71% of Earth and has absorbed around 90% of the extra heat trapped by greenhouse gases.
Hot and cold spots of planet Earth.Persian Gulf in summer: One of the warmest seas on Earth, yet its corals have adapted to heat that would bleach reefs almost anywhere else.
Hot and cold spots of planet Earth.Death Valley record high: Measured at Furnace Creek in July 1913, it is the hottest air temperature officially accepted, though some climatologists dispute it.
Hot and cold spots of planet Earth.Old Faithful's water: The Yellowstone geyser erupts about every 90 minutes, and because of the altitude its water is just short of boiling.
Hot and cold spots of planet Earth.Rhyolite lava: Rhyolite lava is thick and silica-rich, so it traps gas and tends to erupt explosively rather than flow gently.
Hot and cold spots of planet Earth.Basalt lava: Runny basalt builds Hawaii's shield volcanoes and, cooled under the sea, forms most of the ocean floor.
Hot and cold spots of planet Earth.Earth's inner core: This solid iron-nickel ball is about as hot as the Sun's surface, yet crushing pressure keeps it from melting.
Hot and cold spots of planet Earth.Lightning bolt: A bolt heats the air around it to about five times the Sun's surface temperature; the sudden expansion is thunder.

When these acts split up (the first time.Sex Pistols: Their only studio album, Never Mind the Bollocks, came in 1977, and the band broke apart on a chaotic US tour.
When these acts split up (the first time.Led Zeppelin: After drummer John Bonham died in 1980, the band said they couldn't carry on and disbanded, rather than replace him.
When these acts split up (the first time.ABBA: The Swedish group stopped working together after 1982, but a musical built on their songs, Mamma Mia!, later made them huge again.
When these acts split up (the first time.The Smiths: Johnny Marr and Morrissey wrote the songs; the split came after just four studio albums, yet the band's influence runs wide.
When these acts split up (the first time.Nirvana: Kurt Cobain's death in 1994 ended the band, and Dave Grohl went on to form the Foo Fighters.
When these acts split up (the first time.Oasis: After a backstage brawl at a Paris festival in 2009, the Gallagher brothers ended the band, and a reunion followed in 2025.
After 31 years, they parted amicably in 2011, with no drama, and said they were simply done.
When these acts split up (the first time.My Chemical Romance: Their song Welcome to the Black Parade defined emo; they split in 2013, but reunited in 2019.
When these acts split up (the first time.Daft Punk: The French robot duo announced their end with a video called Epilogue in 2021, after 28 years together.

Units of time, short to long.Second: The base unit of time is defined by atomic clocks, using the vibrations of a cesium atom, 9,192,631,770 of them.
Units of time, short to long.Minute: The word comes from Latin 'pars minuta prima', the first small part of an hour, and the split into 60 traces to Babylonian counting.
Units of time, short to long.Hour: Ancient Egyptians split daylight and night into twelve parts each, and that is why our day still runs in two sets of twelve.
Units of time, short to long.Day: A day is the Earth's rotation, and the length gets longer by about two milliseconds a century.
Units of time, short to long.Week: Seven days a week comes from ancient Babylon, with each day named for a classical planet, which still shows in English day names.
Units of time, short to long.Fortnight: The word comes from 'fourteen nights', and it's mostly a British expression now.
Units of time, short to long.Month: Months are tied to the Moon, but Europe's calendar months no longer match its phases, with lengths of 28 to 31 days.
Units of time, short to long.Year: A year of 365 days needs a leap day every four years, because the Earth takes about 365.25 days to orbit the Sun.
Units of time, short to long.Decade: A ten-year stretch, the word comes from Greek deka, and many people remember eras by the decade.
Units of time, short to long.Millennium: A thousand years, from Latin mille, and the turn of the one that began in 2001 was celebrated a year too early by many.

Release years of these Zelda games.The Legend of Zelda: The first cartridge was gold and had a battery to save progress; Miyamoto drew on boyhood cave exploring, and Zelda is the princess, not the hero.
Release years of these Zelda games.A Link to the Past: It introduced the parallel Light and Dark Worlds, a structure that many later games borrowed.
Release years of these Zelda games.Link's Awakening: This Game Boy adventure is set on Koholint Island, not Hyrule, and Link has no Triforce.
Release years of these Zelda games.Ocarina of Time: It brought 3D targeting to the series with Z-targeting and is often ranked among the best games ever.
Release years of these Zelda games.Majora's Mask: The player has three days to stop the Moon from crashing into the world, and can reset time to try again.
Release years of these Zelda games.The Wind Waker: Its cel-shaded cartoon look was controversial at first but has aged beautifully, and the game is about sailing a great sea.
Release years of these Zelda games.Twilight Princess: Link can become a wolf in this darker game, which launched on both GameCube and Wii.
Release years of these Zelda games.Skyward Sword: It was built for Wii MotionPlus, so swinging the controller swings the sword, to mark the series' 25th anniversary.
Release years of these Zelda games.Breath of the Wild: A Switch launch title that let players climb nearly anything and tackle the world in any order.
Release years of these Zelda games.Tears of the Kingdom: Its Ultrahand power lets players glue together vehicles and gadgets from found objects.

When these epic journeys began.Xenophon's Ten Thousand: Xenophon's account, the Anabasis, tells of Greek mercenaries cut off in Persia, who cried 'Thalatta!' on sighting the sea.
When these epic journeys began.Pytheas sails north: The Greek explorer from Massalia sailed to Britain and described a land of the midnight sun he called Thule.
When these epic journeys began.Zhang Qian heads west: The Han envoy spent about ten years as a captive of the Xiongnu, and his trip opened the Silk Road.
When these epic journeys began.Faxian sets out for India: The Buddhist monk walked to India to find scriptures, and wrote a detailed account of the lands he saw.
When these epic journeys began.Xuanzang leaves for India: His journey to India inspired the classic novel Journey to the West, with its monkey king.
When these epic journeys began.Ibn Fadlan to the Volga: The Abbasid envoy described a Viking chieftain's ship funeral on the Volga.
When these epic journeys began.Marco Polo leaves Venice: His book, dictated in a Genoese prison, introduced Europeans to China and Asia.
When these epic journeys began.Ibn Battuta leaves Tangier: He travelled about 120,000 km across Africa and Asia, far more than Marco Polo.
When these epic journeys began.Zheng He's first voyage: Admiral Zheng He's treasure fleet featured giant ships that dwarfed those of Columbus.
When these epic journeys began.Vasco da Gama sails for India: He found the sea route to India around Africa, reaching Calicut in 1498.

When these party games came out.Operation: Inventor John Spinello reportedly sold the idea of the buzzing surgery game for just $500.
When these party games came out.Hungry Hungry Hippos: The four hippos are named Lizzie, Henry, Homer and Harry, and the game is all about who gobbles the most marbles.
When these party games came out.Jenga: Designer Leslie Scott, born in Tanzania, took the name from the Swahili 'kujenga', meaning 'to build'.
When these party games came out.Balderdash: The game of invented definitions descends from an older parlour pastime, 'Dictionary', played with a real dictionary.
When these party games came out.Scattergories: The letter die has just 20 sides, leaving out Q, U, V, X, Y and Z.
When these party games came out.Taboo: The squeaker players hit when a teammate slips on a forbidden word became the game's signature sound.
When these party games came out.Cranium: Two former Microsoft executives in Seattle founded it, and Hasbro bought it in 2008.
When these party games came out.Apples to Apples: Its judge-picks-the-funniest-card format later inspired Cards Against Humanity.
When these party games came out.Dixit: The French designer Jean-Louis Roubira's dreamlike picture-card game won Germany's Spiel des Jahres award in 2010.
When these party games came out.Telestrations: It is a drawing version of Telephone, a pastime also known as 'Eat Poop You Cat', where sketches get hilariously misread.

Japanese companies, by founding year.Mitsubishi: Mitsubishi began as a shipping business in 1870, and its three-diamond logo comes from family crests of its founders.
Japanese companies, by founding year.Seiko: Seiko started as a clock shop in Tokyo, and in 1969 it released the first commercial quartz wristwatch.
Japanese companies, by founding year.Nintendo: Nintendo made hanafuda playing cards in Kyoto before video games, and it still sells such cards today.
Japanese companies, by founding year.Panasonic: Panasonic was founded as Matsushita, and its founder began with a small lamp socket business before growing into a giant.
Japanese companies, by founding year.Toyota Motor: Toyota began as a loom-making company, and the car business was spun off from it, hence the Toyoda spelling change.
Japanese companies, by founding year.Sony: Sony started in a bombed-out Tokyo department store room, as Tokyo Tsushin Kogyo, before changing its name in 1958.
Japanese companies, by founding year.Honda: Honda began by fitting small engines to bicycles, and Soichiro Honda built them himself before launching motorcycles.
Japanese companies, by founding year.Sanrio: Sanrio is the company behind Hello Kitty, which began as a small gift shop business that sold cute goods.
Japanese companies, by founding year.Muji: Muji means no brand quality goods in Japanese, and its shops are known for plain design without logos.
Japanese companies, by founding year.Rakuten: Rakuten means optimism, and it began as an online mall, now one of Japan's biggest e-commerce firms.

A total solar eclipse, step by step.Moon takes a first nibble: First contact is when the Moon first touches the Sun's edge. It begins about an hour or more before totality, and you need eclipse glasses to look.
A total solar eclipse, step by step.Sun shrinks to a crescent: Shaded gaps between leaves act as pinhole cameras, projecting dozens of tiny crescents onto the ground during the partial phase.
A total solar eclipse, step by step.Daylight dims and cools: The temperature can fall by several degrees, and light turns eerie and silvery. Birds may go quiet and some flowers close up.
A total solar eclipse, step by step.Shadow bands ripple: Faint, wavy lines can be seen racing across light surfaces just before and after totality. They are caused by turbulence in the atmosphere.
A total solar eclipse, step by step.Baily's beads sparkle: Named for Francis Baily, the beads of light appear when sunlight shines through valleys at the Moon's edge, just before totality.
A total solar eclipse, step by step.Diamond ring flashes: Just as the last sliver of Sun peeks out, with the corona forming a ring, the effect looks like a sparkling diamond on a ring.
A total solar eclipse, step by step.Totality: corona appears: The Sun's pearly outer atmosphere, normally invisible, becomes visible. Totality lasts only a few minutes at most, and it is safe to look at then.
A total solar eclipse, step by step.Second diamond ring: As totality ends, the diamond ring effect appears again on the opposite side. Eclipse glasses must go back on at this point.
A total solar eclipse, step by step.Crescent Sun returns: Light comes back quickly, and the sky brightens. The partial phase on the way out mirrors the one on the way in.
A total solar eclipse, step by step.Moon slides off: The last contact marks the end, a couple of hours after the first. Total eclipses happen somewhere on Earth about every 18 months.

Changing a flat tyre, step by step.Pull over somewhere safe: Hard shoulders and lay-bys are safest, and driving on a flat can wreck the rim, so slow down gently instead of braking hard.
Changing a flat tyre, step by step.Put on the handbrake: Pairing the handbrake with a low gear or Park stops the car rolling, and on a slope a rock behind a wheel adds a backup.
Changing a flat tyre, step by step.Get out the spare and jack: Many modern cars carry a skinny space-saver spare meant for short distances and limited speeds, often about 50 mph.
Changing a flat tyre, step by step.Loosen the wheel nuts: Nuts are cracked loose while the wheel is still on the ground, because the tyre's grip stops the whole wheel spinning under the wrench.
Changing a flat tyre, step by step.Jack up the car: A jack must sit on the car's reinforced jacking points, since pressing on thin bodywork can crush it or let the car slip.
Changing a flat tyre, step by step.Take off the nuts and wheel: A car wheel with its tyre often weighs 15 kg or more, so slide it straight off the studs rather than lifting it.
Changing a flat tyre, step by step.Fit the spare wheel: Spare tyres lose pressure while they sit unused for years, so it's worth checking the spare's pressure now and then.
Changing a flat tyre, step by step.Hand-tighten the nuts: Starting the nuts by hand lets the wheel seat evenly and avoids cross-threading, which can ruin a stud.
Changing a flat tyre, step by step.Lower the car: The car comes down before the final tightening, because the tyre's weight on the road holds the wheel still against the torque.
Changing a flat tyre, step by step.Fully tighten the nuts: Nuts are tightened in a star pattern, not around the circle, so the wheel pulls flat against the hub. Recheck them after a short drive.

Goldilocks and the Three Bears, in story.The bears go for a walk: Goldilocks first appeared in Robert Southey's 1837 tale, where the intruder was an old woman, not a girl.
Goldilocks and the Three Bears, in story.Goldilocks finds the cottage: She was called Silver-Hair and Silverlocks before the name Goldilocks stuck in the early 1900s.
Goldilocks and the Three Bears, in story.Papa Bear's porridge: too hot: Astronomers borrowed the story for the Goldilocks zone, the orbit where a planet is not too hot or cold for liquid water.
Goldilocks and the Three Bears, in story.Baby Bear's porridge: all gone: Porridge, boiled oats or grain, is among the oldest cooked foods, which makes the bears' breakfast about as ordinary as it gets.
Goldilocks and the Three Bears, in story.Baby Bear's chair breaks: In Southey's 1837 telling, the intruder's rudeness ends with her leaping out a window, not strolling home.
Goldilocks and the Three Bears, in story.Baby Bear's bed: just right: Just right gave rise to the Goldilocks principle, used in economics and medicine for the comfortable middle choice.
Goldilocks and the Three Bears, in story.The bears come home: In Southey's version the bears are a Great Huge Bear, a Middle-sized Bear and a Little Small Wee Bear, and their voices go from deep to tiny.
Goldilocks and the Three Bears, in story.\"Someone's eaten my porridge\": The repeated Somebody's been eating my porridge is a rule of three, which storytellers use to build a pattern before breaking it.
Goldilocks and the Three Bears, in story.The bears find her asleep: The bears finding her asleep is the climax, and different versions have her waking and fleeing in fright.
Goldilocks and the Three Bears, in story.Goldilocks runs away: Versions end with her escaping through a window, falling, or running home, and the tale never settles on a moral.
